finding.title: Extract scheduler_providers.dart's isTaskCompleted to a top-level function so epic_27_story_f5 tests the real code

evidence.quote:
bool _isTaskCompletedBuggy(DailyTask task, List<Completion> completions) {
  return completions.any((c) {

'BUG REPRO: buggy isTaskCompleted returns true for sentinel completion '
          '(this test documents the pre-fix behaviour and must FAIL until F5 is applied)',

finding.why: isTaskCompleted is a private closure declared inside allDailyTasksProvider's @riverpod build function (scheduler_providers.dart:414-427) — it is not importable, so this file hand-copies it into two local mirrors (_isTaskCompletedBuggy / _isTaskCompletedFixed) instead of calling production code. The file's own 'BUG REPRO' test claims it 'must FAIL until F5 is applied' (line 118), but _isTaskCompletedBuggy is a static local function that reproduces the bug unconditionally forever — that claim is false, and `flutter test` confirms all 4 tests pass today regardless of the real source. A real regression to the production sentinel-skip logic would not be caught by this file (though test/features/scheduler/presentation/providers/scheduler_all_daily_tasks_test.dart's 'SP4' test does exercise the real provider and would catch it, so this is false assurance in the acceptance artifact rather than a total coverage gap).
finding.recommendation: Extract the matching predicate at scheduler_providers.dart:414-427 to a top-level pure function (e.g. on SchedulerEngine or a new daily_task_completion_matcher.dart) that both the provider and this test import; delete the hand-copied mirrors. Alternatively delete this file's duplicated logic and move the story_f5 tag onto scheduler_all_daily_tasks_test.dart's SP4 test.
acceptance_criteria: epic_27_story_f5_prior_learning_filter_test.dart imports and calls the production matching function directly; no local re-implementation of isTaskCompleted remains.
`flutter analyze` and the scheduler test suite pass after extraction.

finding.title: Back epic_27_story_27_8's tutor/rules security-boundary tests with real rule evaluation, not substring matching

evidence.quote:
// as Group A — the `fake_firebase_security_rules` package cannot evaluate
  // `request.auth.uid` comparisons dynamically, but string-scanning the rules

finding.why: The file's own comment admits the dynamic rules-emulation package can't evaluate request.auth.uid, so the 'LOAD-BEARING security invariant' tests (line 199) fall back to scanning firestore.rules TEXT for substrings. A rule edit that inserts a bypass while preserving the substrings — e.g. `allow create: if isOwner(uid) || request.auth != null;` — still contains 'isOwner(uid)', still omits 'isTutorOf', and would pass every assertion here while granting any authenticated user write access to completions. Per the audit baseline, the real emulator-based rules suite (firestore_rules.test.mjs) is currently soft-skipped in `make ci` (TQ-9, already known) — so this Dart text-matching suite may be the only thing CI runs today for the tutor-write-block boundary this file calls load-bearing.
finding.recommendation: Assert the tutor-write-block and owner-write invariants against the actual Firestore Rules emulator (@firebase/rules-unit-testing) with real auth contexts (assertFails/assertSucceeds), not string containment on the rules source; keep the text-scan tests only as a fast pre-check, not the sole gate.
acceptance_criteria: An emulator-backed test asserts a tutor-authenticated write to completions/{completionId} is denied and an owner-authenticated write succeeds.
CI runs this test unconditionally (ties into the existing TQ-9 soft-skip fix).

finding.title: Extract a shared FakeFirestoreGateway test helper instead of re-implementing FirestoreGateway in 23 test files

evidence.quote: // W6.13: fetchAuditLogEntries added to FirestoreGateway interface.

finding.why: `grep -rl "implements FirestoreGateway" test/` finds 23 files, of which this ~370-line _ToggleableFakeGateway is one; the other 22 are independent hand-rolled implementations of the same 25+-method interface. This file's own accretion comments ('Step 1 additions', 'W6.13', 'T1.gateway — stub') show the interface has grown at least 3 times since this fake was written — each growth requires editing every one of the 23 fakes or the analyzer fails each independently (classic shotgun surgery). This is also the single largest contributor to the file's AG-3 overage (see the paired finding).
finding.recommendation: Extract one canonical InMemoryFirestoreGateway/FakeFirestoreGateway to test/helpers/, parameterized for online/offline + failure-injection behaviour used here, and have call sites configure it instead of re-implementing the interface.
acceptance_criteria: A shared fake gateway exists under test/helpers/ implementing FirestoreGateway once.
This file's _ToggleableFakeGateway is replaced by (or extends) the shared fake; repo-wide count of independent `implements FirestoreGateway` fakes decreases.

finding.title: Replace epic_27_story_4_widget_golden_test.dart's 'AC structural verification' tautologies with real assertions
finding.why: All three assertions are structurally guaranteed to pass regardless of the real code: (1) a bare class-type literal like `BulkMarkScreen` is never null in Dart — this can only fail if the file doesn't compile; (2) `shapes` at line 345-350 is a locally hardcoded copy of the golden-loop shape list (lines 107-112), fully disconnected from it — deleting 3 of the 4 real `goldenTest('track_card_...)` calls would not fail this test; (3) `expectedLocales` at line 360 is a hardcoded 2-element literal, disconnected from golden_runner.dart — changing that helper to skip the Hebrew variant (exactly what the comment at line 358-359 claims this test guards against) would not fail it either.
finding.recommendation: Replace with real assertions: e.g. have golden_runner.dart expose the locale list / registered test count it actually iterates, and assert against that value, not a local copy; for BulkMarkScreen, either delete the vacuous check or assert something meaningful about its public constructor surface.
acceptance_criteria: The 'AC structural verification' tests fail when the real 4-shape loop or the real he-locale emission in golden_runner.dart is removed/broken.
